clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient presents with stage‑1 hypertension, obesity, and pre‑diabetes, establishing a high‑risk metabolic‑cardiovascular phenotype. Laboratory trends (metabolic alkalosis, low‑normal potassium, rising BUN/Cr) point toward a volume‑contraction state. Because the medication list is absent, an iatrogenic diuretic effect is the most plausible driver and is prioritized. Secondary endocrine hypertension (primary hyper‑aldosteronism) and common contributors such as obstructive sleep apnea are also considered. Essential hypertension and metabolic syndrome are likely background conditions that will coexist. Psychosocial stressors explain the adjustment disorder diagnosis and may worsen adherence.
